xep.header:
Message Retraction — monocles profile
This specification defines a method for indicating that a message should be retracted. This revision is the monocles chat profile of XEP-0424: it keeps the wire format of version 0.5.0 and adds the rules implemented by monocles chat (Android and desktop): end-to-end encrypted retractions (OMEMO and post-quantum OMEMO2), retractions from the sender's other devices, reliable attribution of one's own group chat messages, retractions that arrive before the message they remove, and stricter target-id handling.

0.5.0-monocles1 2026-10-21 am
monocles chat profile; wire format and namespace unchanged from 0.5.0.
Target ids per message type (groupchat, one-on-one, MUC private message); receivers also match the sender's stanza 'id', but never use it for duplicate suppression; retracting a correction retracts the corrected message.
Encrypted retractions: inside the SCE envelope for PQ OMEMO2, authenticated by the encrypted fallback for OMEMO; an encrypted message is only retracted under the same fingerprint, so a server cannot forge a cleartext retraction.
Retractions from the sender's other devices: accepted under another fingerprint of the sender's own account only if that device is trusted, active and listed.
Own group chat messages: attributed by occupant id, archive real JID or live nick, never by an archived nick alone; own messages from other devices are treated as outgoing.
Retractions that arrive before their message (archive paging) are kept, bound to their sender, bounded per conversation, and applied when the message arrives.
One-on-one: only the author's side may retract or correct a message.
Forged moderations are discarded; local cleanup rules; no time limit.

section1.p: A chat participant might want to retract a message which they've already sent out, for example if they've mistakenly sent it to the wrong recipient or groupchat.

Due to the federated and extensible nature of XMPP it's not possible to remove a message with full certainty and a retraction can only be considered an unenforceable request for such removal. Clients which don't support message retraction are not obligated to enforce the request and people could have seen or copied the message contents already.

(monocles) This document is the monocles profile of XEP-0424. It keeps the wire format and the namespace of version 0.5.0 unchanged, so any 0.5.0 implementation interoperates with it, and it adds the rules that monocles chat implements. They matter most where XEP-0424 meets end-to-end encryption, multi-device use and message archives: a retraction that is accepted too easily lets someone delete other people's messages, and one that is rejected too easily leaves a message visible that its author wanted gone. Text added by this profile is marked "(monocles)".

(monocles) In this document, a user's own side is everything the user's account sent, from any of its devices: messages sent by this client, &xep0280; sent carbons and archived copies of messages sent by another device of the same account, and the user's own messages reflected by a &xep0045; room.

If a client implements message retractions, it MUST specify the 'urn:xmpp:message-retract:1' feature in its service discovery information features as specified in &xep0030; and the Entity Capabilities profile specified in &xep0115;.

Similarly, a server that is aware of message retractions and will therefore ensure that they're archived for later retrieval (e.g.via &xep0313;), MUST also advertise the 'urn:xmpp:message-retract:1' feature.

example.caption: Client requests information about a chat partner's client
Partner's client advertises support for retraction

section1.p: A client, server or other service (for example a &xep0045; service) MAY enforce a time limit on message retractions, meaning that it will only honour a retraction request that it receives within a certain amount of time after the original message was sent. An entity which enforces such a limit SHOULD advertise it in its service discovery information response, by including a &xep0128; data form with a FORM_TYPE of 'urn:xmpp:message-retract:1' and a 'max-age' field, the value of which MUST be the limit in seconds.

example.caption: A groupchat service advertises a retraction time limit of 30 minutes

section1.example: <iq type='result' to='romeo@montague.example/orchard' from='muc.capulet.example' id='info2'> <query xmlns='http://jabber.org/protocol/disco#info'> ... <feature var='urn:xmpp:message-retract:1'/> ... <x xmlns='jabber:x:data' type='result'> <field var='FORM_TYPE' type='hidden'> <value>urn:xmpp:message-retract:1</value> </field> <field var='max-age'> <value>1800</value> </field> </x> </query> </iq>
section1.p: (monocles) monocles clients enforce no time limit and therefore advertise no 'max-age' field. They honour retractions of messages of any age, as the Time limits rules ask of an entity without a limit.
Consider a situation where a user sends a message to the wrong recipient:

example.caption: The user's client sends a message to the wrong recipient

section1.example: <message type='chat' to='lord@capulet.example' id='wrong-recipient-1'> <body>Have not saints lips, and holy palmers too?</body> </message>
section1.p: The author notices that the message was sent to the wrong recipient and indicates to their client that it should be retracted.
The client sends out a retraction message and uses the 'id' attribute of the <message> element in the original message to indicate that it should be removed.
In the case of a group chat message, for example &xep0045;, instead of the message ID, the XEP-0359 stanza ID that was assigned by the group chat SHOULD be used.

example.caption: The client sends out a retraction

section1.example: <message type='chat' to='lord@capulet.example' id='retract-message-1'> <retract id="wrong-recipient-1" xmlns='urn:xmpp:message-retract:1'/> <fallback xmlns="urn:xmpp:fallback:0" for='urn:xmpp:message-retract:1'/> <body>/me retracted a previous message, but it's unsupported by your client.</body> <store xmlns="urn:xmpp:hints"/> </message>
section1.p: It's RECOMMENDED that you include fallback text in the <body/>, so that servers will archive the retraction and non-supporting clients can still indicate that there was an intent to retract. When a <body/> is included, it SHOULD be marked with a &xep0428; <fallback/> element with a 'for' attribute set to 'urn:xmpp:message-retract:1', to indicate that it merely serves as a fallback. The fallback text is intentionally generic and SHOULD NOT identify or repeat the contents of the retracted message, since doing so would undermine the purpose of the retraction. Additionally, you SHOULD include a &xep0334; <store/> hint, to ensure that the retraction is archived even by services that are unaware of this specification.

(monocles) monocles clients always send the <fallback/> element, a generic fallback body and the <store/> hint. They send only the 'urn:xmpp:message-retract:1' form: neither the &xep0422; fastening form nor 'urn:xmpp:message-retract:0' is sent. When the conversation is end-to-end encrypted, the retraction is encrypted too, see Encrypted Retractions.

It might be desirable to remove the retracted message from a &xep0313; service, while still recording the fact that it once existed, in order to aid clients in synchronizing their archives. To do this, the archiving service MAY replace the retracted message contents with a 'tombstone'.
A service which supports tombstones MUST advertise the 'urn:xmpp:message-retract:1#tombstone' feature in its Service Discovery responses.

example.caption: Client requests service discovery information from the server
The server advertises support for tombstone retraction

section1.p: When replacing the original message with a tombstone, the original contents (i.e. the <body/> and any related elements which might leak information about the original message) get replaced with a <retracted/> element which MUST include an 'id' attribute that's set to the value of the retraction's <message/> element's 'id' attribute, so that clients can match the tombstone to the retraction (which MUST also be stored in the archive).
The <retracted/> element SHOULD also include a 'stamp' attribute indicating the time at which the retraction took place.
As with other XEP-0313 archived messages, the &xep0203; <delay/> element is used to indicate when the original message was received.

example.caption: Retracted message tombstone in a MAM result

section1.example: <message id='aeb213' to='lord@capulet.example/chamber'> <result xmlns='urn:xmpp:mam:2' queryid='f27' id='stanza-id-1'> <forwarded xmlns='urn:xmpp:forward:0'> <delay xmlns='urn:xmpp:delay' stamp='2019-09-20T23:08:25Z'/> <message type='groupchat' from='romeo@montague.example' to='lord@capulet.example' id='wrong-recipient-1'> <retracted stamp='2019-09-20T23:09:32Z' xmlns='urn:xmpp:message-retract:1' id='retract-message-1'/> </message> </forwarded> </result> </message>

section1.p: A receiving client can choose to remove the retracted message from whatever display is used for messages, from any stored history, or choose to display the fact that a message has been retracted in another way.

A MUC or other service that supports message retraction SHOULD prevent further distribution of the message by the service (e.g., by not replaying the message to new occupants joining the room, omitting the message from history archive requests where possible, or replacing the original message with a 'tombstone').

Some clients may have been offline while the retraction was issued. The archiving service therefore MUST store the retraction message, regardless of whether the original message is deleted or replaced with a tombstone. These clients will then become aware of the retraction as soon as they catch up with the archive.
A client MAY inform the user that a no-longer displayed message did previously exist and has been removed.
Supporting clients MUST set a unique 'id' on the <message> element in outgoing stanzas (as per &xep0359;), to make them suitable for retraction.

The Sender MUST NOT send a retraction request for a message with non-messaging payloads, in other words, for a message that serves as a transport for protocol signalling and is not displayed as a message to the user. For example, a sender MUST NOT send a retraction for a roster item exchange request (&xep0144;) or a file transfer part. Conversely, a message that conveys user-visible content is considered to have a messaging payload even when that content is not contained in the <body/> element itself. For example, a &xep0447; message, in which the <body/> merely serves as a fallback, MAY be retracted.

A retraction message's <body/> serves only as a fallback for clients that don't support this specification, and its contents are entirely under the sender's control. A sender which includes a <body/> SHOULD mark it with a &xep0428; <fallback/> element with a 'for' attribute set to 'urn:xmpp:message-retract:1' (see the Use Case section).

A client that supports this specification MUST NOT display the <body/> of a message containing a <retract/> element, whether or not the <body/> is marked with a XEP-0428 fallback indication. This also applies when no message matching the 'id' of the <retract/> element can be found: instead of rendering the sender-supplied fallback text, the client MAY indicate that the sender attempted to retract an unknown message.

A retraction (that's not part of a &xep0425; operation) MUST only be processed when both the original message and the retraction request are received from the same bare-JID (in a one-on-one conversation) or full-JID (in a non-anonymous MUC from &xep0045;).
When used in a semi-anonymous MUC, the recipient client MUST check that a message retraction was sent by the author of the retracted message by checking the occupant id from &xep0421;.

(monocles) A retraction never becomes a message of its own: it is not stored, shown, counted as unread or notified, whether or not it was applied. In a one-on-one conversation a retraction (and a correction) MUST come from the same side as the message: the peer knows the id of every message the user sent, but MUST NOT be able to retract or correct one of them, even an unencrypted one. The user's own side covers all of the user's devices. The rules in the following sections refine the sender checks above. A retraction MUST pass all of them before it is applied.

section2.p: Before sending a retraction request, a client SHOULD determine whether any involved entity (for example the group chat service in a group chat, or the chat partner's client in a one-on-one chat) advertises a retraction time limit, as described in Discovering support, and SHOULD NOT offer retraction of a message older than the smallest advertised limit.

An entity which receives a retraction request for a message older than its advertised limit MAY ignore the request. An entity which doesn't enforce and advertise such a limit SHOULD honour retraction requests regardless of the age of the retracted message, in order to provide behaviour that's consistent across implementations.

For messages of type 'groupchat', the ID assigned to the stanza by the group chat itself must be used. This is discovered in a <stanza-id> element with a 'by' attribute that matches the bare JID of the group chat, as defined in &xep0359;.
If a group chat does not support &xep0359;, a client can still opt to include an <origin-id> element in the message stanza, which can be used to refer to the message in a retraction.
For other message types the sender should use the value of the 'id' attribute on the <message> element. See however the Security Considerations below.

ul.li: for a groupchat message: the room's <stanza-id by='room@service'/>, or its <origin-id/> when the room assigned none;
for a one-on-one message: the message 'id'. monocles clients set it equal to the <origin-id/> on their own messages;
for a MUC private message: the message 'id'. Some clients (including monocles chat for Android) send no <origin-id/> on private messages.

section2.p: (monocles) A receiver looks the target up among the messages of the same conversation by the <origin-id/>, by the archive- or room-assigned <stanza-id/>, and (outside groupchats) by the sender's message 'id' when it differs from the <origin-id/>. The message 'id' MUST only be used to find a retraction or correction target, never to detect duplicate messages. Message ids need not be unique (see Uniqueness of message IDs), and treating them as unique would drop unrelated messages. A match is still only a candidate: the sender checks in the following sections decide.

(monocles) A retraction whose 'id' is that of a &xep0308; correction retracts the corrected message, including the original and all its corrections. A correction is never left as a visible remainder of a retracted message.

section1.p: (monocles) In an end-to-end encrypted conversation the retraction itself is encrypted with the conversation's encryption.

(monocles) With post-quantum OMEMO2 (the monocles OMEMO-PQXDH profile of &xep0384;, namespace 'urn:monocles:omemo-pq:1'), the <retract/> element, its <fallback/> and the fallback <body/> are placed inside the &xep0420; envelope's <content/>. The outer stanza carries only the encrypted element, the OMEMO fallback body, the <store/> hint and the EME hint. A receiver MUST NOT act on a cleartext <retract/> next to an OMEMO2 <encrypted/> element.

example.caption: A PQ OMEMO2 retraction: the decrypted SCE envelope

section1.example: <envelope xmlns='urn:xmpp:sce:1'> <content> <retract xmlns='urn:xmpp:message-retract:1' id='wrong-recipient-1'/> <fallback xmlns='urn:xmpp:fallback:0' for='urn:xmpp:message-retract:1'/> <body xmlns='jabber:client'>This message has been retracted by the sender.</body> </content> <rpad>…</rpad> <time stamp='2026-10-21T10:15:00Z'/> <from jid='juliet@capulet.example'/> <to jid='romeo@montague.example'/> </envelope>
section1.p: (monocles) With legacy OMEMO (&xep0384; 0.3), which encrypts only the body, the <retract/> element stays in cleartext and the encrypted fallback body authenticates the retraction. The retraction's fingerprint is the fingerprint that decrypted that body.
(monocles) A receiver MUST apply the following fingerprint rule, in addition to the sender checks of the Business Rules:

ul.li: A message that was received unencrypted may be retracted by a retraction from its sender, encrypted or not.

A message that was received encrypted MUST only be retracted by an encrypted retraction whose fingerprint equals the message's fingerprint. A cleartext retraction (which the sender's or the receiver's server could forge) MUST NOT remove an encrypted message.

There are two exceptions. The sender's other devices may retract it under the conditions in Retractions from the Sender's Other Devices. A moderation by the room may retract it under the conditions in Moderation.

section1.p: (monocles) The same rule applies to &xep0308; corrections. A correction that fails it is not applied, and a retraction that fails it is ignored.

section1.topic: Retractions from the Sender's Other Devices
section1.p: (monocles) A user who sends a message from the phone and retracts it on the desktop sends a retraction under a different OMEMO fingerprint than the message carries. Both devices belong to the same account, so the retraction is legitimate, but the strict fingerprint rule would reject it. It is accepted under these conditions:

ol.li: Both the retracted message and the retraction are on the receiver's own side (see Introduction). In a group chat that requires the proof of Own Messages in Group Chats for both.
The retraction is encrypted. A cleartext own-side retraction still needs a matching fingerprint, so a server cannot forge one.
Its fingerprint belongs to an OMEMO identity of the user's own bare JID that the receiver trusts: blindly trusted (BTBV) or verified, but not undecided or untrusted.
That identity is active. If the receiver knows the account's current device list, the device is also listed in it.

section1.p: (monocles) Successful decryption alone is no proof of any of this, because implementations decrypt messages from undecided and replaced identities too. The same conditions apply to corrections.

(monocles) The user's own messages sent from another device arrive as &xep0280; sent carbons, as &xep0313; results or as room reflections. A receiver SHOULD store them as outgoing messages already sent, so the user can also correct and retract them from this device. Such a message keeps the fingerprint of the device that sent it.

(monocles) In a group chat, every client of the user receives the user's messages reflected by the room under the user's nick. A receiver has to decide whether such a message is really the user's, because that decision lets it retract (and correct) the user's own messages. A message from the user's nick is the user's own only if one of these holds:

ul.li: its &xep0421; occupant id equals the user's own occupant id, as reported by the room in the user's own presence;
it arrived live and the room assigns no occupant id that contradicts it. While the user is joined, the room keeps nicks unique among the occupants present.

section1.p: (monocles) A nick alone MUST NOT make an archived message the user's. While the user was away, someone else may have joined under the same nick. In a room without &xep0421; their messages would otherwise appear as the user's and could retract the user's messages. When the occupant id is known it decides, even against a matching nick. A client MUST NOT learn its own occupant id from a message that is not proven its own by one of the rules above. The user's own presence remains the authority.

(monocles) A proven own message sent from another device is stored as an outgoing message (see Retractions from the Sender's Other Devices). With OMEMO2, a client never encrypts a message to the device that sends it. A client therefore decrypts an encrypted reflection only if it was sent by another device of the user's account and wraps a key for this device. Its own reflections keep the locally stored plaintext, and they only fill in the room's stanza-id.

(monocles) Archives are usually paged backwards, from the newest result to older ones. A retraction then often arrives before the message it removes, and the message is shown when it arrives a page later. The same happens when a client misses the live room reflection of its own message: its copy lacks the room's stanza-id that the retraction addresses.

(monocles) A receiver MAY therefore keep a retraction whose target it cannot find, together with its sender binding: the direction (own side or not), the occupant id, the fingerprint, and whether it qualified as an own-device retraction. When a message with a matching id arrives later, the receiver applies the retraction only if the message passes the same checks as a live retraction would. That includes a message that turns out to be a duplicate of a copy the receiver already has, in which case the existing copy is retracted.

(monocles) A receiver MUST keep retractions of the same id from different senders apart. If it kept only one per id, someone else's retraction of that id, which fails the sender check later, could displace the author's, and the message would stay visible.

(monocles) The receiver SHOULD store such a message as a tombstone rather than drop it. Paging the same archive range again then recognises it as a duplicate and does not bring it back. It is never notified or counted as unread.

(monocles) Pending retractions cost the sender nothing, so a receiver MUST bound them. monocles clients keep at most 500 per conversation and drop the oldest. monocles chat desktop stores them with the conversation; monocles chat for Android keeps them in memory while it runs, which covers paging through an archive.

(monocles) A &xep0425; moderation is announced by the room itself, from its bare JID, as a <retract/> carrying a <moderated/> element. A <retract/> that carries <moderated/> but does not come from the room's bare JID is forged and MUST be discarded. It MUST NOT be treated as the sender's own retraction instead.

(monocles) A genuine moderation may remove an encrypted message regardless of its fingerprint, because the room cannot know it. It addresses the message by the room's stanza-id. A moderation that arrives before its message (archive paging) MAY be remembered by that stanza-id, so the message is never stored.
(monocles) A client that applies a retraction, whether received or its own, keeps a hidden or "retracted" tombstone of the message, or removes it entirely, and in either case removes its content:

ul.li: the body, the attachment and any corrections, the reply reference and the fingerprint are cleared;
a notification still shown for the message is removed;
a locally stored file or thumbnail of the message is deleted, and a live location shared in it ends.

section1.p: (monocles) Files the message pointed to on an &xep0363; upload service are not deleted, because the protocol offers no way to do so. See Privacy Considerations.

There can never be a guarantee that a retracted message was never seen or otherwise distributed, and it is encouraged for clients and services when possible to inform users that no such guarantee exists.

If message retraction results in the complete removal of any record of the original message's body, for example to be replaced by a tombstone, then this could be used to hide messages that moderators might want to be notified of.
To prevent message spoofing, it's very important that the sender's JID or XEP-0421 occupant id of message retractions are checked (as explained in the Business Rules section).

section2.p: The fallback <body/> of a retraction message is entirely under the sender's control, and a sender could deliberately place content in it that's unrelated to the retraction. Clients that support this specification won't display it, while non-supporting clients will display it verbatim, meaning that different recipients may see very different content for the same message. While this divergence is inherent to &xep0428; fallbacks in general, message retraction makes it easy to trigger deliberately: combined with a <retract/> element that refers to a nonexistent message, it could be used to send content which is only visible to some recipients, or which disappears without a trace on others.

For this reason, clients that support this specification MUST NOT render the <body/> of a retraction message, also when the referenced message can't be found (see the Business Rules section), and senders MUST set fallback text that describes the retraction, as shown in the Use Case section.

Clients that don't support &xep0359; (and therefore don't support &xep0424;), are not guaranteed to have a unique 'id' attribute on their <message> elements. This means that when someone is using a supporting client, and attempts to retract a message from a different, non-supporting client, it might not be possible to uniquely indentify the message being retracted, as more than one message could have the same 'id' attribute.

To mitigate this, clients can do a &xep0030; request to check if the other client supports XEP-0359, and if not, they can choose to not support retraction for messages from that client, or otherwise warn the client about this limitation. However, the other client might not be online to respond to a disco request, so this is not a foolproof method.

(monocles) For the same reason, a receiver never uses the message 'id' to suppress duplicates (see Using the correct ID). Even when two messages share an id, the sender checks keep a retraction from reaching anyone else's message.

(monocles) Without the fingerprint rule of Encrypted Retractions, a server could delete any end-to-end encrypted message by injecting a cleartext retraction under the sender's JID. The own-device exemption is limited to encrypted retractions from trusted, active, listed devices of the user's own account. A compromised or merely announced device whose identity the user has not trusted therefore gains nothing. It also never applies to other people's messages.

(monocles) Nicks are only unique among the occupants present at a time. The rules in Own Messages in Group Chats keep someone who used the user's nick from being treated as the user, whether to retract the user's messages, to have their own messages shown as the user's, or to plant a wrong own occupant id.

(monocles) A remembered retraction carries the same sender binding as a live one, so it cannot be used to remove someone else's message that arrives later under the same id. It cannot remove the user's own copy either when the later message merely reuses the user's id. Because retractions are kept per sender, a third party cannot cancel the author's retraction by retracting the same id first. Keeping pending retractions bounded protects storage from floods of retractions for ids that never arrive.

section1.p: (monocles) A retraction removes the message from supporting clients and, with tombstones, from archives. It does not remove files uploaded with &xep0363;. Whoever received the link, or obtained it from a copy of the message, can keep downloading such a file until the upload service expires it. With OMEMO, the file itself is encrypted and its key travelled only in the encrypted message.

(monocles) This profile changes no element, so it interoperates with any 0.5.0 implementation. Their cleartext retractions of cleartext messages work unchanged. Their retractions of encrypted messages are applied if they are encrypted under the message's fingerprint. A 0.5.0 implementation without the own-device rule may reject a retraction made on another device of the sender.

(monocles) monocles chat for Android and monocles chat desktop implement the same rules: encrypted retractions with the fingerprint rule and the own-device exemption, the target ids (a MUC private message is retracted with a private message, by its message id), the side check, pending retractions and the 'urn:xmpp:message-retract:1' feature. Android also advertises 'urn:xmpp:message-retract:0' and still understands the fastening-based form of older clients. Two differences remain. The desktop client attributes its own group chat messages by the rules in Own Messages in Group Chats. Android also accepts the room's per-occupant user record for live messages. And as noted under Retractions Before Their Message, Android keeps pending retractions in memory only.
None.

section2.p: The ®ISTRAR; includes 'urn:xmpp:message-retract:1' in its registry of protocol namespaces (see &NAMESPACES;).

&xep0068; defines a process for standardizing the fields used within Data Forms qualified by a particular namespace. The following field is registered for use within Service Discovery extension elements:
